article_title: The Impact of NBA Math Hoops on Students' Math Achievement: A Randomized Controlled Trial
citation: McKinney, D., Walters, K., Powell, K., Sabalburo, E., & Morton, C. (2026). The impact of NBA Math Hoops on students' math achievement: A randomized controlled trial. WestEd. https://www.wested.org
title: NBA Math Hoops
description: NBA Math Hoops is a STEM learning program developed by Learn Fresh in partnership with the NBA and WNBA, built around an interactive board game using real player statistics. "As they play an interactive board game and complete associated lessons built around real NBA and WNBA player statistics, students have opportunities to build fluency in arithmetic, fractions, decimals, percentages, and data analysis." The program includes 10 supporting lessons and has reached over 1.4 million students across all 50 states since 2012.
requirements: Requires teacher training (2-3 hours) covering game rules, lesson review, and implementation planning
Requires board game materials, player cards, and 10-sided dice
constraints: Materials and shipping costs are covered by Learn Fresh for participating programs
target_learning_goals: Math fluency in arithmetic, fractions, decimals, percentages
examples: In the RCT, students played the board game in pairs, computing sums, differences, products, and quotients of two 10-sided dice rolls to select shot locations and player cards with real shooting statistics
key_sources: McKinney, D., Walters, K., Powell, K., Sabalburo, E., & Morton, C. (2026). The impact of NBA Math Hoops on students' math achievement: A randomized controlled trial. WestEd. https://eric.ed.gov/?id=ED681343

article_title: Ten tips to harnessing generative AI for high-quality MCQS in medical education assessment.
citation: Magzoub Mohi Eldin, Zafar Imran, Munshi Fadi, Shersad Fouzia. (2025). Ten tips to harnessing generative AI for high-quality MCQs in medical education assessment. Medical Education Online. https://doi.org/10.1080/10872981.2025.2532682
title: A twelve-item checklist for reviewing AI-generated MCQs, adapted from the NBME item-writing guide
description: Table 2 presents a yes/no checklist for technically reviewing AI-generated items, partially adapted from the NBME Item-Writing Guide. It checks that the stem is a direct question, options are homogenous, logically ordered, free of repeats, opposites, ineffective or overly long options, unintended clues, vague or absolute words, negative stems, and ALL/NONE of ABOVE options. The article positions it as a quality check instrument for the first level of review.
requirements: Used within a technical review of all item components including stem, lead-in question, and options
constraints: Partially adapted from the NBME item-writing guide, so its items reflect that source's item-writing flaw conventions
target_learners: medical educators and item writers reviewing AI-generated items
target_learning_goals: detection of technical item-writing flaws in AI-generated MCQs
examples: Checklist items include whether there are any unintended clues in the stem/options and whether the stem is phrased negatively
key_sources: Magzoub Mohi Eldin, Zafar Imran, Munshi Fadi, Shersad Fouzia. (2025). Ten tips to harnessing generative AI for high-quality MCQs in medical education assessment. Medical Education Online. https://doi.org/10.1080/10872981.2025.2532682

article_title: An e-Problem-Based Learning Program for Infection Control in Nursing Homes: A Quasi-Experimental Study.
citation: Choi Young-Rim, Lee Ye-Na, Kim Dayeong, Park Won Hee, Kwon Dai Young, Chang Sung Ok. (2022). An e-Problem-Based Learning Program for Infection Control in Nursing Homes: A Quasi-Experimental Study. International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health. https://doi.org/10.3390/ijerph192013371
title: Network-Based Instructional System Design (NBIS) model development process
description: The program was developed following the "Network-Based Instructional System Design model", a five-step process of analysis, design, production, implementation, and evaluation. In this application, analysis involved needs interviews with nine nursing home practitioners and a literature review; design set goals, content, multimedia materials, and chatbot support; production created storyboards and Chrome-optimized software; implementation ran guided training meetings and a two-week web deployment; evaluation used a critical thinking disposition measure.
requirements: Needs analysis with practitioners and literature review to set goals and content
Technical support (e.g., chatbot) for learner–educator communication
constraints: Program was optimized for the Chrome environment only
target_learners: Nursing home nursing staff in workplace training
target_learning_goals: Infection control competence via critical thinking disposition
examples: Pilot-tested over two weeks before implementation
